- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is positive (≥0.30) and price is trending upward, model frequently overcorrects; cap upward forecasts at 10–15% above recent high.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative, model underestimates downward moves; add 2–5% buffer to downward forecasts to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10–14-day moving average of recent prices.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.00–0.10), model tends to overreact; apply a “sentiment dampening” factor to reduce forecast volatility.
